newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's Fransabank said to sell 5 pct of shares.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's Fransabank said to sell 5 pct of shares.

text.p: Lebanon's Fransabank is planning to sell five percent of its shares in a deal worth up to $25 million, a Beirut finance house that is arranging the deal said on Friday.
"We are making preparations for the bank to sell the shares. Many investors from Europe, the United States and Lebanon and a few from the Gulf are interested," said an official from Lebanon Invest.
He said the deal would be worth between $20 million and $25 million.
Fransabank is not listed on the official Beirut Stock Exchange or the over-the-counter market but it is closely watched by brokers.
"Fransabank has a lot of growth potential," said one broker.
Fransabank raised its mid-year net profit by 36.5 percent in 1997 to 28.12 billion Lebanese pounds ($18.26 million) over the same period of 1996.
Its shareholders' equity rose by 40.47 percent in the first half of the year to 151.37 billion pounds.
Lebanon Invest was founded in 1995 and initially grouped more than 65 shareholders, including companies and Arab businessmen.
